title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the continuation of 'La Longue Marche' (pp. 650bis-787), Grothendieck studies a discrete group Pi_0, typically a Teichmueller or mapping-class-type group, possibly SL(2,Z). He studies it through a 'schematic envelope' Pi, an affine group scheme over Spec Z whose generic fibre Pi_Q is an algebraic envelope (hull) of Pi_0, with a canonical map Pi_0 -> Pi(Z). T_0 ~= Z is the 'twist' group. The homomorphisms k_i : T_0 -> Pi_0, one per 'genre' i, are the Dehn-twist-type embeddings. On the previous page he postulated that each K_i extends schematically to a homomorphism k_i^! : T_0 -> Pi. Here T_0 is a group scheme over Z attached to T_0, presumably G_a or a model of it. Generically, k_i^! agrees with K_i up to a positive rational rescaling r_i. He also assumed that on Z-points it factors through Pi_0.

On this page he works 'on integral Lie groups, i.e. over Spec Z'. Take all the k_i^!, for all i and all Pi_0-conjugates of the k_i. Pass to Lie algebras: Lie(k_i^!) : Lie(T_0) ~= Z -> Gamma Lie(Pi) ~= Lie(Pi). These maps are non-canonical.

He then adds a hypothesis: these maps are 'universal monomorphisms', i.e. their images exhaust the Lie algebra. The conclusion is that the global Lie algebra Gamma Lie(Pi) is generated as a Z-MODULE, not merely as a Lie algebra, by the images of a generator of T_0. Concretely, the I elements log(twist_i) in Lie(Pi), together with all their Ad(Pi_0)-conjugates, span the lattice Lie(Pi).

The following page integrates this statement. The identity component Pi^0, viewed as an etale sheaf on the big etale site of Spec Z, should be generated by finitely many of the subgroups k'_i(G_0). Pi itself should be generated by these together with the constant group (Pi_0)_{S_0}. He then asks whether the relations of Pi_0 plus the compatibility square (57) suffice as a presentation.

Margin: 'this hypothesis seems unreasonable as soon as Pi_0 = SL(2,Z), but one can't help it!'

In modern terms, this is an integrality / Z-model condition on the Lie algebra of an algebraic (relative or Zariski) envelope of a mapping class group: the Lie lattice should be the Ad(Pi_0)-span of logarithms of Dehn twists.
errors: Over Q the condition is natural. The Q-span of the Ad(Pi_0)-orbit of the twist logarithms is Ad(Pi)-stable by Zariski density, hence an ideal. It is therefore everything as soon as Pi_Q is generated by the one-parameter subgroups. The real content is integral, namely whether the Z-span is the whole lattice Lie(Pi) and not just a sublattice of finite index. The text does not discuss this distinction or the effect of the rescalings r_i on it.

For Pi = SL_2 over Z, conjugating e=(0 1;0 0) by SL(2,Z) gives (-ac, a^2; -c^2, ac). These elements already span sl_2(Z) over Z (they give e, f, and h). So the hypothesis is not unreasonable for the naive envelope SL_2/Z. The margin's doubt must concern a larger envelope of SL(2,Z), e.g. a relative or pro-algebraic completion, which is huge because SL(2,Z) is virtually free and lacks the congruence subgroup property. Which envelope is meant is not made explicit on this page.

Several words are illegible, notably the sentence beginning 'Je ...' and the phrase 'en dépendant'. The precise logical chain between 'universal monomorphisms' and Z-module generation is therefore only partly recoverable.

ideas.what: Integral (Spec Z) model of the algebraic envelope of a discrete group (mapping class / Teichmueller group), with schematic extensions of the Dehn twist maps T_0 -> Pi_0 to one-parameter subgroups T_0 -> Pi
ideas.modern_name: Integral models of relative/Malcev/weighted completions of mapping class groups; unipotent one-parameter subgroups through Dehn twists
ideas.usually_credited_to: Relative completion of mapping class groups: Hain (1990s); weighted completion: Hain–Matsumoto (2000s). Integral versions are much less developed.
ideas.where_published: Teichmueller tower and Dehn twists appear in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche. Schematic Z-envelopes of this form: unsure.

ideas.what: Hypothesis that the Z-Lie algebra of the envelope is the Z-span of the Ad(Pi_0)-conjugates of the logarithms of the twists (one per 'genre')
ideas.modern_name: Lie algebra spanned by Dehn-twist logarithms; integral generation of Lie algebras of completions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Over Q, generation of relative-completion Lie algebras by twist logarithms is implicit in Hain's work. The integral span condition has no standard reference that I know.

ideas.what: Global version: Pi^0, as a sheaf on the big etale site of Spec Z, is generated by finitely many twist subgroups, and Pi by these plus the constant group Pi_0. Question whether the relations of Pi_0 plus the compatibility squares give a presentation.
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of a group scheme by a discrete group and one-parameter subgroups (amalgam-type presentation of the envelope)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an integral (over Z) generation condition for the envelope of a mapping-class-type group: the Lie lattice should be spanned by Pi_0-conjugates of Dehn-twist logarithms. He flags it as doubtful for SL(2,Z) and does not resolve it. An integral theory of such completions, and whether twist logarithms span an integral lattice, is largely absent from the literature, which works over Q or Q_l.
missed.quote: on conclut que ΓLie(Π) est engendré (en tant que Z-module) par les images ... d'un générateur de T_0 ... cette hyp. semble déraisonnable dès qu'on a Π_0 = SL(2,Z), mais on n'y peut ... !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral structures on relative/weighted completions of mapping class groups bear on integral Galois actions on them and on the integrality of motivic Lie algebras.

missed.claim: Envelopes of mapping class groups built from Dehn-twist one-parameter subgroups prefigure Hain's relative completion (and its unipotent elements coming from twists). They do so in a Z-integral, sheaf-theoretic (big etale topos) setting that Hain's work does not attempt.
missed.quote: les homs correspondants sur les algèbres de Lie (56) Lie(k_i^!) : T_0 → ΓLie(Π) ≃ Lie(Π)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests an integral refinement of relative completion that could interact with the Grothendieck–Teichmueller program over Z.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an unpublished, unresolved hypothesis on integral envelopes of mapping class groups that anticipates relative completion. It is speculative, explicitly self-doubted, and only partly legible, with no finished result.
transcription_corrections: 'k_i : \hat{\pi}_0 [?] → Π_0' is most likely 'k_i : T_0 → Π_0' (the twist group), consistent with (55) and (56).
In (56) the source is the group scheme T_0 (underlined) with Lie(T_0) ≃ Z; the '≃ Z' under T_0 refers to the Lie algebra/group being identified with Z.
Margin likely reads: 'cette hyp. semble déraisonnable dès qu'on a Π_0 = SL(2,Z), mais on n'y peut rien !'
'les I éléments' likely means one element for each of the I genres i ∈ I.
